picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 1.82 mph, home -0.19 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 209 measured fastballs; home over 243 measured fastballs); a gap of 2.02 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)

picks.evidence_tier_label: More than one system agrees, or one system's signal cleared its hardest threshold.
picks.thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) top_minus_bottom -- this lineup's top-of-order minus bottom-of-order strength (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.034 wOBA, home 0.000 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,676 plate-appearance denominators; home over 7,045 plate-appearance denominators); a gap of 0.033 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.023 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,838 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a top-heavy order concentrates its best bats where the extra plate appearances go, and club-level pricing averages that concentration away; the weakest mechanism of the six, kept because V4 stated it before seeing its result. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome e7f41ed66082c279.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_velocity_gap -- how far the opposing starter's fastball sits above league pace (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 1.82 mph, home -0.19 mph (this game's own values rest on: away over 209 measured fastballs; home over 243 measured fastballs); a gap of 2.02 mph, clearing the threshold of 1.96 mph (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,149 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a starter whose fastball sits above league pace is holding stuff the season line has not caught up to, so the lineup facing the harder thrower is the disadvantaged side; velocity leads results and the market prices results. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)

picks.evidence_tier_label: More than one system agrees, or one system's signal cleared its hardest threshold.
picks.thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) top_minus_bottom -- this lineup's top-of-order minus bottom-of-order strength (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 0.034 wOBA, home 0.000 wOBA (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,676 plate-appearance denominators; home over 7,045 plate-appearance denominators); a gap of 0.033 wOBA, clearing the threshold of 0.023 wOBA (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,838 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a top-heavy order concentrates its best bats where the extra plate appearances go, and club-level pricing averages that concentration away; the weakest mechanism of the six, kept because V4 stated it before seeing its result. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome e7f41ed66082c279.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 28.6%, home 75.0% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 46.4 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 33.4 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 11da2d044a08ac38.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 40.0%, home 71.4% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 31.4 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 40.0%, home 71.4% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 31.4 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 40.0%, home 71.4% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 31.4 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 40.0%, home 71.4% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 31.4 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 40.0%, home 71.4% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 31.4 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 55.1%, home 44.2% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,481 batted balls; home over 1,075 batted balls); a gap of 10.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 66fd4a5e38e890fd.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 55.1%, home 44.2% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,481 batted balls; home over 1,075 batted balls); a gap of 10.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 66fd4a5e38e890fd.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 57.1%, home 85.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 28.6 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 55.1%, home 44.2% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,481 batted balls; home over 1,075 batted balls); a gap of 10.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 66fd4a5e38e890fd.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 57.1%, home 85.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 28.6 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 55.1%, home 44.2% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,481 batted balls; home over 1,075 batted balls); a gap of 10.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 66fd4a5e38e890fd.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 57.1%, home 85.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 28.6 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 55.1%, home 44.2% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,481 batted balls; home over 1,075 batted balls); a gap of 10.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 57.1%, home 85.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 28.6 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 55.1%, home 44.2% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,481 batted balls; home over 1,075 batted balls); a gap of 10.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 66fd4a5e38e890fd.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 57.1%, home 85.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 28.6 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 55.1%, home 44.2% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,481 batted balls; home over 1,075 batted balls); a gap of 10.9 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 66fd4a5e38e890fd.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 57.1%, home 85.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 28.6 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 4703ed67882a9d2b.)

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

basis: case strength: distinct families backing the selection (a family contributes at most one, so near-duplicate systems cannot manufacture agreement), then how much of the genome's own mechanism claim fired and at what threshold rung, then board depth and freshness, then price standing as the final tiebreak. Price standing is execution quality and never predictive merit: the consensus is derived from the same prices, so their difference can never be evidence the market is wrong.

picks.thesis: Backing the away side of h2h because 1 pre-registered signal fired: (1) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 34.9%, home 46.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 1,348 batted balls; home over 90 batted balls); a gap of 11.7 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 11.6 percentage points (rung 2 of 3, the 75th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the away side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). (Strategy: evolab genome 44faa9639a3a54e8.)

picks.evidence_tier_label: Multiple independent systems agree, at the strongest signal they check for.
picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 3 pre-registered signals fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 37.5%, home 66.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 29.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. (2) primary_pitch_share -- the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 31.9%, home 42.0% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,396 pitches; home over 9,672 pitches); a gap of 10.1 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. (3) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 51.9%, home 40.8% (this game's own values rest on: away over 576 batted balls; home over 1,618 batted balls); a gap of 11.1 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md). picks.thesis: Backing the home side of h2h because 3 pre-registered signals fired: (1) lineup_platoon_share -- the share of the posted lineup holding the platoon advantage over the starter it faces (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 37.5%, home 66.7% (this game's own values rest on: away over 9 lineup slots; home over 9 lineup slots); a gap of 29.2 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 22.2 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,856 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: the classic exploitation: a lineup posted one-handed against a starter it holds the platoon advantage over gets more of its plate appearances in the favourable split than the club-level season line the market prices ever reflects. (2) primary_pitch_share -- the share of pitches the opposing starter throws with his single most-used offering (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 31.9%, home 42.0% (this game's own values rest on: away over 3,396 pitches; home over 9,672 pitches); a gap of 10.1 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 9.7 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 4,061 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at +1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism favours), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: concentration in one pitch is predictability: the more of a starter's arsenal is a single offering, the more of the lineup's preparation transfers, and pitch-level lean is not a term in any club-level price. (3) starter_groundball_share -- the opposing starter's career ground-ball share (each side's number describes the matchup that side's own lineup faces): away 51.9%, home 40.8% (this game's own values rest on: away over 576 batted balls; home over 1,618 batted balls); a gap of 11.1 percentage points, clearing the threshold of 6.5 percentage points (rung 1 of 3, the 50th percentile of that gap over the ladder's derivation sample, 3,516 games with both sides measured, 2023-24). This mechanism's direction was frozen before any search ran at -1 (the side holding more of it is the side the mechanism harms), so the signal points to the home side. Pre-registered reason it should matter: a career ground-ball starter takes the air out of an offence that lives on balls in the air, so the lineup facing the higher ground-ball share is the disadvantaged side and club-level pricing averages the collision out. This is a signal count, not a forecast: the genome publishes no calibrated probability, so p_model is null and edge_bps is null by construction. Nothing here says the market's price is mistaken, and no claim of value is attached to it -- no such claim has been earned (docs/PREREG_CALIBRATED_PROBABILITY.md).
